1.why: All seven screenshots show static, sparse pages with no animation, moving images, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary actions are solid blue buttons and the current step is bolded and highlighted, though the dark activity-log box and multiple colored callouts also compete for attention.

3.why: Each page presents one labeled input and one main button near the top with help consistently placed below, so the needed controls are quick to locate.

4.why: The persistent six-step progress list and visible password checklist externalize steps and rules, although users must still absorb rules such as 'codes expire after 15 minutes and can only be used once.'

5.why: No screen offers a remember-me checkbox, autofill hint, or password-manager option; only plain email, password, and code fields are shown.

6.why: Completed steps turn green in the sidebar and the same header, help panel, and Resume recovery button repeat on every page, letting the user recognize familiar and saved progress.

7.why: Most sentences are short and plain, but occasional jargon like 'short-lived and single-use' approval and 'synthetic demonstration identifier' reduces readability.

8.why: No error state appears in any screenshot, only green success/info banners, so whether error messages describe the problem and fix could not be observed.

9.why: Step 1 provides a sample identifier (helena.demo@hospital.test) and the simulated delivery shows the exact code format to paste, though the password fields get only a checklist rather than an example.

10.why: The available alternatives ('I know my password — sign in', manual code entry versus 'Open simulated recovery link') are distinct, clearly labeled buttons, even though no face-login option exists.

11.why: Each screen limits decisions to one primary action plus at most two secondary buttons and the sidebar pause/resume pair, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: Every action is followed by an explicit green outcome banner, e.g. 'New password saved securely. Next, confirm your security code.'

13.why: A 'Help and safe sign-in' panel with a 'Show a short reminder' button appears on every step, alongside per-step explanatory notes.

14.why: 'Back to recovery request', the reassurance that 'Nothing happens until you choose Verify code', and the ability to request a new code allow easy retry, though an explicit after-error retry screen is never shown.

15.why: Header, progress sidebar, help panel, button styles, and banner colors are identical across all seven steps, making the design consistent and learnable.
